stage_description: The end-of-life stage is the period when chronic or incurable disease limits quality of life. Care centers on palliative support: pain relief, comfort, appetite, and preserving the animal's dignity. An honest quality-of-life assessment with the veterinarian and a timely, humane decision are essential to prevent suffering.
nutrition: Feed to appetite: warm, aromatic food, easy access to the bowl, and vet-prescribed appetizing or therapeutic diets if needed. The priority is enjoyment of food and adequate hydration rather than strict dietary targets.
activity: Gentle, short activity as the animal wishes; a comfortable warm bed, non-slip surfaces, and help with mobility. The goal of this stage is comfort and calm companionship, not physical exertion.
veterinary_check_frequency: Frequent veterinary contact to manage pain and symptoms on an individualized palliative-care plan, sometimes weekly or more often. A hospice plan and objective quality-of-life criteria are discussed.
dental_care: Gentle mouth care for comfort; painful dental procedures are deferred unless they improve well-being. Offer soft or moist food if the mouth is sore.
warning_signs: Refusing food and water, uncontrolled pain, labored breathing, loss of control over elimination, and complete apathy. These signs call for an urgent quality-of-life discussion with the veterinarian.
disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and does not replace consultation with a veterinarian.
